'''Julia Elizabeth Bergner''' is a mathematician specializing in [[algebraic topology]], [[homotopy theory]], and [[higher category theory]]. She is a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Virginia]].{{r|uva}}

==Education and career==
Bergner graduated from [[Gonzaga University]] in 2000.{{r|cv}} She completed her Ph.D. at the [[University of Notre Dame]] in 2005. Her dissertation, ''Three Models for the Homotopy Theory of Homotopy Theories'', was supervised by [[William Gerard Dwyer]].{{r|cv|mgp}}

After postdoctoral research at [[Kansas State University]], she joined the mathematics faculty at the [[University of California, Riverside]] in 2008. She moved from there to the [[University of Virginia]] in 2016.{{r|cv}}

==Selected publications==
Bergner is the author of the book ''The homotopy theory of'' ({{math|∞}},1)''-categories'' (London Mathematical Society Student Texts 90, Cambridge University Press, 2018).{{r|hti1c}}

==Recognition==
In 2018, the [[Association for Women in Mathematics]] gave Bergner the [[Ruth I. Michler Memorial Prize]] for her research on [[algebraic K-theory|algebraic {{mvar|K}}-theory]].{{r|michler}}
